topStories.headline: 28 Businesses Win Grants as Inner Sunset's Homegrown Revival Fund Picks Its First Class
topStories.dek: SF New Deal announced the winners of the Inner Sunset Neighborhood Vibrancy Fund on Thursday, with an Oakland pizza institution and a new Yemeni café set to fill the neighborhood's most prominent vacancies.
topStories.body:
Two long-empty storefronts at the corner of 9th Avenue and Irving Street — arguably the Inner Sunset's busiest intersection — are finally getting new tenants, thanks in part to a $300,000 fund seeded entirely by anonymous local neighbors. The nonprofit SF New Deal announced on Thursday the 28 recipients of the Inner Sunset Neighborhood Vibrancy Fund, a pilot program launched in July that extends the kind of small-business support once reserved for downtown to a residential commercial corridor.

The most closely watched award goes to Mama's Boy Pizza, the NYC-style slice shop from Oakland, which is set to take over the former Reliable Rexall Pharmacy space — vacant for over a year — with an expected spring opening. The lease was made possible with a grant of up to $20,000, the top tier the fund offers for businesses moving into vacant storefronts. Across the street, city Planning Department records show BMO Bank is eyeing the former Bank of America space.

Nearly 100 local businesses applied for grants that ranged from $5,000 for technical assistance to $20,000 for vacant-storefront takeovers, and up to $10,000 for storefront beautification. Among the other recipients is 403 Coffee, slated to open at 403 Irving St. The family behind the produce stand KJ Produce on Irving Street is also among those supported, planning to open a Yemeni café this winter.

SF New Deal executive director Simon Bertrang described the Inner Sunset as precisely the kind of neighborhood the program was designed to serve. The fund's backers are hoping it becomes a replicable model for other San Francisco commercial corridors.

topStories.headline: Beloved Burmese Spot Closes on Irving; World-Renowned Naples Pizza Chef Opens Today in Its Place
topStories.dek: Inle Burmese Cuisine has shuttered for health reasons after three years in the Inner Sunset, while Vincenzo Capuano — a celebrated Neapolitan pizza maker — opens his first U.S. restaurant at the same address today.
topStories.body:
The Inner Sunset's restaurant row saw a significant turn this week. Inle Burmese Cuisine, which had operated at 822 Irving St. near Ninth Avenue since relocating from Noe Valley in early 2023, closed its doors on Sunday. Co-owner Morgan Sue said the closure is an open-ended break while the owners address health issues, and the restaurant may return in some form in the future.

Sue and his family immigrated from Burma to the United States in 1998. He got his start in the restaurant industry at Nan Yang, one of the oldest Burmese restaurants in the Bay Area, before opening Inle in October 2019 — just months before the pandemic. Despite the difficult timing, the restaurant built a loyal neighborhood following and had been a rare local outpost of Burmese cuisine.

The news arrives alongside a significant opening at the same stretch of Irving. Vincenzo Capuano, a world-renowned Neapolitan pizza chef, is opening an eponymous pizzeria at 822 Irving today — his first restaurant in the United States. The owners held a soft-opening neighborhood party last Sunday before the official October 23 debut.

The back-to-back closure and opening captures the pace of commercial churn that has come to define the Inner Sunset in recent years: high turnover at individual storefronts, but consistently fast replacement driven by demand from both residents and new operators drawn to the corridor.

topStories.headline: Eleven Days Out: What a Yes or No on Prop G Would Actually Mean for the Sunset
topStories.dek: With the November 3 vote approaching, the Controller's price tag — nearly $10 million upfront — and a list of park features that would have to be torn out are sharpening the stakes for Sunset and Parkside residents.
topStories.body:
For the third time in four years, San Francisco voters will weigh in on the Upper Great Highway when they go to the polls on November 3. Proposition G, placed on the ballot after supporters gathered more than 15,000 valid signatures, would reopen the two-mile stretch of roadway between Lincoln Way and Sloat Boulevard to private vehicles Monday through Friday, while keeping it closed to cars from Friday evening through Monday morning and on holidays.

The measure seeks to reverse Proposition K, which voters approved in November 2024 and which converted the former roadway into Sunset Dunes Park. Prop G supporters, organized under the group Great Highway for Everyone, argue that routing traffic off the coastal road has pushed vehicles onto nearby Sunset neighborhood streets and increased injury rates. District 4 Supervisor Alan Wong has publicly backed the weekday-reopening approach.

The San Francisco Controller's Office has put a number on the trade-off: roughly $9.8 million in one-time capital costs to convert the park back to a road, plus between $500,000 and $1.9 million annually for ongoing maintenance, traffic signals, and sand removal. That estimate will appear on the official voter information pamphlet.

On the ground, passage would require removing park features that have been added since the closure, including a skate park opened in 2025 and a pirate-themed playground that debuted in September 2026. The San Francisco Chamber of Commerce has declined to take a position on the measure. Voters in the Sunset and Parkside, who live closest to the roadway and split sharply on Prop K two years ago, are once again expected to be a decisive constituency.

events.title: Inner Sunset Monthly Neighborhood Cleanup
events.location: Meet at the Emporium, Irving St. at 8th Ave., Inner Sunset
events.description: The Inner Sunset Park Neighbors host their regular fourth-Saturday cleanup from 10am to 12pm. Volunteers meet in front of the Emporium on Irving at 8th Avenue to pick up supplies before spreading out through the neighborhood streets.

events.title: 44th Annual Sandcastle Classic at Ocean Beach
events.location: Ocean Beach (near Balboa St.), Outer Sunset
events.description: Leap Arts in Education hosts Northern California's largest sandcastle competition, with teams of students, architects, engineers, and designers building giant sculptures on the sand. Free to watch; the event runs through approximately 3:30 PM.

events.title: The Great Hauntway at Sunset Dunes
events.location: Sunset Dunes Park, Judah–Taraval stretch, Ocean Beach
events.description: The 6th Annual Great Hauntway brings Halloween trick-or-treating to the Sunset Dunes oceanfront promenade from 1–4 PM along the Judah-to-Taraval section of the park. Candy volunteers can sign up through Friends of Sunset Dunes.

events.title: Final Ocean Beach Bonfire Weekend of 2026
events.location: Ocean Beach fire rings, Outer Sunset
events.description: The last legal bonfire weekend at Ocean Beach before the annual No Burn Season begins November 1. The fire rings will not be available again until March 1, 2027, so Saturday, October 31 is the final evening of the season.

events.title: Inner Sunset Flea Market — Season Finale: The Big Lunch & Annual Pie Contest
events.location: Irving St. between 9th and 11th Ave., Inner Sunset
events.description: The 11th season of the Inner Sunset Flea Market closes out with its annual themed finale featuring The Big Lunch and the Pie Contest. Free admission; two blocks of vendors, live music, and family-friendly activities run from 10am to 4pm.

events.title: District 4 Family Summit
events.location: Sunset Recreation Center, 2201 Lawton St., Outer Sunset
events.description: The San Francisco Department of Children, Youth & Their Families hosts a free listening session for families in the Outer Sunset, Parkside, and surrounding neighborhoods as part of the city's first Citywide Community Needs Assessment. Free food, childcare, and interpretation services are provided; runs 11am–1:30pm.

moreNews.headline: Board of Supervisors Passes Street-Tree Fee Ordinance Co-Sponsored by D4's Alan Wong
moreNews.body: The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted 7-4 in early September to allow smaller development projects to pay a $2,590-per-tree in-lieu fee rather than planting street trees, as part of Mayor Daniel Lurie's PermitSF permitting-reform initiative. The ordinance, co-sponsored by District 4 Supervisor Alan Wong, also exempts accessory dwelling units from street-tree requirements entirely and curtails some public appeals of city-initiated hazardous-tree removals. Supporters say the change lets the city pool funds and target planting in neighborhoods with sparse canopy; opponents argue it will reduce the total number of new street trees planted. The Sunset Beacon examined the ordinance's local impact in its October 18, 2026 edition.

restaurants.name: Savor

restaurants.name: Tadaima
restaurants.description: Minimalist Japanese café on Irving with a calming green-toned interior, specialty matcha drinks, and unique lattes with a devoted neighborhood following.

restaurants.name: Ushi Taro Ramen
restaurants.description: Cozy ramen shop near 9th and Irving praised for its rich Traditional Paitan broth and one of the Sunset's best vegan ramen bowls.

restaurants.name: Ebisu

restaurants.name: Marnee Thai (9th Ave)
restaurants.description: Family-owned Thai restaurant since 1985, celebrating its 40th anniversary and winner of SFGate Best Thai Food 2026, with Thai Select certification for authentic flavors.

restaurants.name: Marnee Thai (Irving St)
restaurants.description: The Outer Sunset branch of the beloved family-owned Thai institution, serving bold traditional flavors on Irving Street for over four decades.

restaurants.name: San Tung
restaurants.description: Beloved neighborhood institution famous for dry-fried chicken wings and handmade northern Chinese noodles, with lines still forming out the door on open days.

restaurants.name: Lavash
restaurants.description: Authentic Persian cuisine served in a charming parklet decorated with greenery and fresh flowers on Irving Street.

restaurants.name: Mezze and Mooore II

restaurants.name: Perilla
restaurants.description: Widely regarded as the best-value Vietnamese food in the Inner Sunset, with generous portions and a loyal neighborhood following.

restaurants.name: Manna
restaurants.description: A small mom-and-pop Korean spot on Irving dishing out bibimbap, tofu stew, spicy noodles, and kimchi-braised pork.

restaurants.name: Maggie & Mac's
restaurants.description: A lively full-bar American restaurant in the former Social Kitchen space at 9th and Irving, drawing early praise for its French dip, meatloaf, and cocktails.

restaurants.name: Arizmendi Bakery
restaurants.description: Worker-owned cooperative since 2000 serving rotating daily pizzas, artisan breads, pastries, and organic coffee just two blocks from Golden Gate Park.

restaurants.name: The Red Tail
restaurants.description: Stylish wine bar on Irving Street open until 11 p.m., filling a long-standing gap in the neighborhood's after-dinner scene.

restaurants.name: Yancy's Saloon
restaurants.description: Old-school dive bar with dart boards, multiple TV screens for sports, and a spacious interior beloved by neighborhood regulars for decades.

restaurants.name: Outerlands
restaurants.description: A landmark Outer Sunset restaurant near Ocean Beach known for fresh-baked bread, Dutch baby pancakes, and inventive seasonal fare under current owner Riley Bartlett.

restaurants.name: Hook Fish Co.
restaurants.description: Sustainably sourced seafood served as burritos, tacos, poke, and fish-and-chips two blocks from Ocean Beach, with a popular outdoor parklet.

restaurants.name: Two Pitchers Brewing
restaurants.description: Outer Sunset craft brewery sharing space with Maillards Smash Burgers, with a parklet patio and a convivial neighborhood atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Sunset Cantina
restaurants.description: Lively corner spot with ample indoor and outdoor seating, happy hour specials, deep-fried avocado tacos, and mezcal margaritas.

restaurants.name: Andytown Coffee Roasters
restaurants.description: Founded in 2014 on Lawton Street, this Outer Sunset institution roasts small-batch coffee in-house and is famous for its signature Snowy Plover espresso drink.

restaurants.name: Dumpling Kitchen
restaurants.description: Beloved Parkside dumpling institution on Taraval with consistently long waits for its fresh, flavorful handmade dumplings.

restaurants.name: Golden Boy Pizza
restaurants.description: Parkside outpost of the legendary 1978 North Beach pizzeria, serving thick focaccia-based square slices with toppings like garlic-clam and pesto vegetable.

restaurants.name: Galinette
restaurants.description: Well-regarded neighborhood restaurant on Taraval with French and Mediterranean influences, drawing diners from across the city.

restaurants.name: House of Pancakes
restaurants.description: Popular Taraval Street spot for Chinese-style savory pancakes and casual all-day breakfast fare, consistently packed through midday.

restaurants.name: New Taraval Cafe
restaurants.description: A reliable neighborhood diner on Taraval Street serving hearty breakfasts and lunches with a loyal local following.

hotels.name: Ocean Park Motel
hotels.description: San Francisco's oldest motel, built in 1937 in Streamline Moderne style with a nautical theme, portholes, a hot-tub courtyard, free parking, and ocean air two blocks from the beach.

hotels.name: Seal Rock Inn
hotels.description: A San Francisco fixture since 1959 perched at Point Lobos overlooking Sutro Baths and the Pacific Ocean, with a recently reopened French-bistro restaurant under chef Alfred Schilling.
hotels.address: 545 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA 94121

hotels.name: The SeaScape Inn
hotels.description: A modestly updated budget motel at the western end of the N-Judah line, steps from Ocean Beach and the Sunset Dunes park.

hotels.name: Ocean Inn
hotels.description: Straightforward budget accommodations in the Outer Sunset within easy reach of Ocean Beach and the N-Judah streetcar.
hotels.address: 1010 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA 94121

hotels.name: Motel 6 San Francisco – Great Highway
hotels.description: No-frills motel on the Great Highway steps from Ocean Beach and adjacent to the Sunset Dunes linear park opened in 2025.

shops.name: Case For Making
shops.description: Outer Sunset creative supply shop specializing in custom watercolor supplies and hands-on process-based workshops for all ages.

shops.name: Ambiance
shops.description: One-stop shop for trendy women's apparel and accessories on Irving Street, a reliable neighborhood fashion destination.

shops.name: San Franpsycho

shops.name: Pepperjack Provisions

shops.name: Fung Tai Framing & Gallery
shops.description: Parkside framing shop and gallery with a strong community reputation for quality, affordability, and attentive service.

artEntertainment.name: Marrow Gallery
